analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. It bumps the 'Last updated' date on line 3 to 2026-10-21 and adds a paragraph at head lines ~715-719 on required/named tool_choice for Qwen 3.5-family checkpoints. The paragraph says they accept the inferred `.qwen35` parser or `.xmlFunction`, and that both concrete Qwen3.8-27B builds, including the embedded-MTP one, advertise forced tools via ToolChoiceEnforcementPolicy.swift. The supplied head excerpt (unit :6) covers only head lines 1-403, so the added lines were not visible as numbered text. I reviewed the patch hunk and found no security-relevant control changes. Nothing was changed in code, keys, attestation, encryption, the E2E path, the cache, or authorization. Related threat IDs checked: T-008, T-041, TB-002 and TB-007. None are affected by this documentation-only change. Coverage limits: the actual ToolChoiceEnforcementPolicy.swift behavior is not in the supplied evidence, so I could not verify that the claim matches the code. Any tool-choice enforcement bug would be a separate code-change question. The documentation drift is not itself a security regression. The base units :4 and :5 are unchanged context for this PR (the base range changes only line 3), so I raised no pre-existing issues.
